findings.comment: Transformer pads lack specific dimension callouts verifying minimum 5-foot clearance from building faces, structures, and foundations. All five transformer pads must be dimensioned on the site or electrical plan to confirm compliance with UCM § 1.10.4.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) identifies five transformer pads on the site. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows these pads in relation to buildings and site features. However, NO dimension callouts or annotations specify the clearance distance from any transformer pad to any building face, structure, or foundation. Visual inspection of the scaled plans suggests the pads are immediately adjacent to or within feet of building edges, but without explicit dimensions, compliance with the minimum 5-foot clearance cannot be verified.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 requires minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from buildings, structures, and building foundations (with limited exceptions for brick/masonry buildings with AE Design written approval). The absence of dimension callouts showing these clearances is a deficiency. The burden is on the applicant to affirmatively demonstrate compliance through specific measurements on the plans. Missing required clearance documentation constitutes non-compliance.

findings.comment: Transformer pad clearances from buildings are not dimensionally documented on the plans. No dimension lines or clearance callouts are shown to verify the 5-foot minimum horizontal clearance from buildings and building foundations. Provide dimension annotations on the electrical plan clearly showing the minimum 5-foot clearance from each building, or reference AE Design-approved pad detail sheets demonstrating compliance.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) shows 5 transformer pads without dimension callouts or clearance annotations. Visual analysis of the 1" = 20' scale drawing estimates distances: Pad 1 approximately 30-40 feet from Bldg 1; Pad 2 approximately 15-20 feet from Bldg 2; Pad 3 approximately 10-15 feet from Bldg 8; Pad 4 approximately 5-10 feet from both Bldg 4 and Bldg 5; Pad 5 approximately 10-15 feet from Bldg 7. No explicit dimension lines, measurement annotations, or written clearance specifications are shown on the plans. No reference to AE Design-approved pad detail sheets that would specify minimum clearance compliance.
findings.reasoning: While visual estimates suggest some pads may comply with the 5-foot minimum clearance requirement (Pads 1, 2, 3), the plans do NOT include actual dimension lines or clearance annotations to definitively confirm the requirement is met. The conservative pass/fail logic requires affirmative evidence (dimension callouts or clearance markings) that the requirement is met, not visual estimation. Pad 4, at approximately 5-10 feet from two buildings, is particularly ambiguous without precise dimensions. The applicant must demonstrate compliance through documented dimensions, not visual approximation.

findings.comment: Transformer pads lack dimension callouts verifying minimum 2-foot clearance from back of sidewalks where sidewalks are adjacent. Provide specific clearance dimensions on site plan.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad NW of Building 1 (adjacent to entry sidewalk)
Transformer pad W of Building 2 (adjacent to sidewalk)
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows multiple sidewalk and walkway features throughout the site, including 5-foot concrete sidewalks along the entry drive and 4-foot decomposed granite walkways between buildings. Transformer pads are located in proximity to these sidewalks. However, no dimension callouts specify the distance from any transformer pad to the back of any sidewalk. The requirement is minimum 2 feet from back of sidewalks.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 requires transformer pads to be located minimum 2 feet from back of sidewalks. The absence of specific dimensions showing this clearance on the site plan is a deficiency. Multiple sidewalks are shown near transformer locations, requiring verification of compliance.

findings.comment: Transformer pads positioned adjacent to pedestrian sidewalks (Pads 1, 2, 3) lack documented clearance dimensions from the back of the sidewalks. Provide dimension lines and callouts on the electrical plan showing the minimum 2-foot clearance from the back of sidewalks to each transformer pad, or demonstrate through AE Design approval that the configuration meets code.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows Pads 1, 2, and 3 each positioned immediately adjacent to pedestrian sidewalks running around the building perimeter. Visual analysis at 1" = 20' scale estimates these pads are approximately 2-5 feet from the back of the sidewalk. No dimension callouts are provided to document the exact clearance from the back of the sidewalk to the pad edge. The code requires 'minimum 2 feet from back of sidewalks,' but the plans do not explicitly annotate this clearance.
findings.reasoning: While the visual estimate suggests the pads may be at or near 2 feet from the sidewalk (meeting the minimum), the plans provide no dimensional annotation to confirm this. Conservative pass/fail logic requires documented evidence (dimension lines/callouts) that the 2-foot minimum is met, not visual estimation. The pads appear to be within or very close to the sidewalk setback zone, creating ambiguity about whether they meet the 2-foot requirement.

findings.comment: Transformer pads lack documentation of minimum 10-foot hot-stick use area clearance on access door side. All five pads require dimension callouts confirming clearance to open area or adjacent buildings.
findings.observation: The electrical plan (Sheet 21) shows five transformer pads with hatched rectangles representing the pad footprint. However, no dimension callouts or annotations indicate the hot-stick use area clearance (the access door side). Sheet 9 shows these pads are located in constrained areas immediately adjacent to buildings, driveways, and other site features. No specific dimensions document a 10-foot minimum clearance from the access door side to open area or adjacent building/structure.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 specifies the hot-stick use area (access door side) must have minimum 10-foot clearance to open area or adjacent building/structure. This is a fundamental access requirement for equipment operation. Without documented dimensions, compliance cannot be verified. The constrained locations visible on the site plan suggest this clearance may not be met, but explicit dimensions are required to make a determination.

findings.comment: Hot-stick use area clearances (minimum 10 feet from access door side) are not documented on the electrical plan. For each transformer pad, clearly indicate which side the access door is located on and provide dimension callouts showing the minimum 10-foot clearance to open area or adjacent building/structure. Verify compliance with AE Design specifications.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 does not document the direction of transformer access doors for any of the five pads, nor does it show the required 10-foot hot-stick use area clearance. Visual analysis shows: Pad 1 is approximately 2-5 feet from a sidewalk curb edge and approximately 5-10 feet from the main entry drive; Pad 4 is approximately 5-10 feet from Buildings 4 and 5 on both sides; Pad 5 is approximately 2-5 feet from a parking drive lane. The regulations require a 10-foot clearance from the access door side to open area or adjacent building/structure. Without documented access door orientation and clearance dimensions, compliance cannot be verified.
findings.reasoning: The code specifies that the hot-stick use area (access door side) must have minimum 10-foot clearance to open area or adjacent building/structure. The plans do not identify which side of each pad is the access door side, nor do they document the clearance distance. Pads positioned 5-10 feet from buildings or 2-5 feet from sidewalks/parking areas may violate this requirement if the access door faces the nearby structure. The burden is on the applicant to document both access door location and clearance verification.

findings.comment: Transformer pads lack dimension callouts verifying minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from water lines. Provide specific clearance dimensions on electrical or utility plan.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows the transformer pad locations and includes blue line symbols representing 'Underground Electric Line.' The sheet references Sheet 19 for utility tap profiles showing water service connections. The plan indicates an 8-inch water line serves the site from Valley View Road. However, no specific dimension callouts on Sheet 21 or the electrical plan documents the horizontal clearance distance between any transformer pad and the water line serving the buildings. The requirement is minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 2.9.1.B.2 requires minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance between transformer pads and water lines. The water utility is shown on the site plans (noted as being 8 inches from Valley View Road per the Engineer's Summary Letter). Without specific dimensions showing the 5-foot clearance distance, compliance cannot be verified. Missing required clearance documentation constitutes a deficiency.

findings.comment: Minimum 5-foot horizontal clearances from transformer pads to water service lines are not dimensionally documented. Provide dimension callouts on the utility and electrical plans showing the minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from each transformer pad to all water service lines, measured from pad edge to pipe centerline or outer diameter.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations relative to water service lines
findings.observation: Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) shows water line routing (-W- designated lines) and Sheet 21 shows transformer pad locations and electric lines. Both sheets depict utilities and pads in close proximity throughout the site, but no specific dimension callouts or clearance measurements are provided between the water lines and transformer pads at any location. The plans do not document horizontal clearance distances required to verify the minimum 5-foot separation.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 2.9.1.B.2 requires minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from transformer pads to water lines. The utility and electrical plans show both utilities on the same sheets but provide no dimensional annotation to verify clearance compliance. Conservative pass/fail logic requires documented evidence (dimension lines/callouts) that the 5-foot minimum is met, not general visual indication of separation.

findings.comment: Transformer pads lack dimension callouts verifying minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from wastewater lines. Provide specific clearance dimensions on electrical or utility plan.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) identifies transformer pad locations. The plan references Sheet 19 for utility tap details and profiles. Sheet 19 shows wastewater service connections from the existing 8-inch wastewater line. However, no specific dimension callouts document the horizontal clearance between any transformer pad and the wastewater service line. The requirement is minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 2.9.1.B.2 requires minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance between transformer pads and wastewater lines. The wastewater utility routing is shown on the plans but clearance distances are not dimensioned. Missing required clearance documentation constitutes a deficiency.

findings.comment: Minimum 5-foot horizontal clearances from transformer pads to wastewater service lines are not dimensionally documented. Provide dimension callouts on the utility and electrical plans showing the minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from each transformer pad to all wastewater service lines, measured from pad edge to pipe centerline or outer diameter.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations relative to wastewater lines
findings.observation: Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) shows wastewater line routing (-WW- designated lines) and Sheet 21 shows transformer pad locations and electric lines. Both sheets depict utilities and pads, but no specific dimension callouts or clearance measurements are provided between wastewater lines and transformer pads. The plans do not document horizontal clearance distances required to verify the minimum 5-foot separation.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 2.9.1.B.2 requires minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from transformer pads to wastewater lines. The utility and electrical plans show both utilities on the same sheets but provide no dimensional annotation to verify clearance compliance. Conservative pass/fail logic requires documented evidence (dimension lines/callouts) that the 5-foot minimum is met.

findings.comment: Transformer pads lack dimension callouts verifying minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from storm drain lines. Provide specific clearance dimensions on electrical, storm sewer, or site plan.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows transformer pad locations and references Sheet 19 for profiles. Sheet 12 (Storm Sewer Plan) shows the proposed storm drainage infrastructure. The storm drain system is illustrated on the site plan with 'SD' symbols indicating storm drain inlets and piping. However, no specific dimension callouts on the electrical plan, storm sewer plan, or site plan document the horizontal clearance distance between any transformer pad and the storm drain system. The requirement is minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 2.9.1.B.2 requires minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance between transformer pads and storm drain lines. While the storm drainage is depicted on the plans, the required clearance dimensions are not provided. Missing required clearance documentation constitutes a deficiency.

findings.comment: Minimum 5-foot horizontal clearances from transformer pads to storm drain lines are not dimensionally documented. Provide dimension callouts on the storm sewer and electrical plans showing the minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from each transformer pad to all storm drain lines, measured from pad edge to pipe centerline or outer diameter.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations relative to storm drain lines
findings.observation: Sheet 12 (Storm Sewer Plan) and Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) show storm drain infrastructure (-SD- designated lines) and transformer pads on the site. Both drawings depict utilities and pads in close proximity, particularly near the northeastern portion where the biofiltration/detention pond and storm infrastructure are concentrated. No dimension callouts or clearance measurements are provided between storm drain lines and transformer pads to document compliance with the minimum 5-foot separation requirement.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 2.9.1.B.2 requires minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from transformer pads to storm drain lines. The storm and electrical plans show both utilities on coordinated sheets but provide no dimensional annotation to verify clearance compliance. Conservative pass/fail logic requires documented evidence (dimension lines/callouts) that the 5-foot minimum is met.

findings.comment: Transformer pads lack dimension callouts verifying minimum 12-inch horizontal and vertical clearance from other underground utilities. Provide comprehensive utility clearance documentation on plans.
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows multiple underground utilities including water, storm drain, and electrical lines labeled on the plan. Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows transformer pad locations and underground electric lines. The plans depict various utility lines throughout the site, but no specific dimension callouts show the 12-inch minimum horizontal and vertical clearance required from transformer pads to other underground utilities (beyond the gas, water, wastewater, and storm drain already cited separately). Missing clearance documentation for other utilities such as reclaimed water, communications, or other underground infrastructure.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.A requires minimum 12-inch horizontal and vertical clearance from transformer pads to other underground utilities (except gas, fuel, steam which have higher requirements, and except the water/wastewater/storm drain which have 5-foot requirements). Without specific dimension callouts for all utilities, compliance cannot be verified. Missing required clearance documentation is a deficiency.

findings.comment: Minimum 12-inch horizontal and vertical clearances from transformer pads to other underground utilities are not documented. Provide detail cross-sections and dimension callouts showing the minimum 12-inch clearance from each transformer pad to all other underground utilities (conduits, telephone, cable, etc.), including both horizontal and vertical separations measured from pad edge to utility centerline or outer diameter.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations relative to other underground utilities
findings.observation: Multiple utility sheets show water, wastewater, storm drain, and electric utility routing. However, no cross-utility dimension callouts are provided showing the minimum 12-inch horizontal and vertical clearance between transformer pads and other underground utilities (conduits, telephone, cable, reclaimed water, etc.). The utility tap plan and electrical plan show general routing but lack specific clearance documentation between different utility types adjacent to transformer pad locations.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.A requires minimum 12-inch horizontal and vertical clearance from transformer pads to other underground utilities (except gas, fuel, steam - which have different clearance requirements). Without dimensional annotation on the plans documenting these clearances at specific locations where utilities cross or run parallel to transformer pads, compliance cannot be verified.

findings.comment: Cross-section drawings showing vertical clearances at all transformer pad access paths are not provided. Submit cross-section drawings for each transformer pad location demonstrating minimum required vertical clearance for equipment access.
codeCitations: UCM § 1.10.3 (survey requirement as required by AE Design)
applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations with overhead structures or enclosed access paths
findings.observation: The site plan set (39 sheets) includes plan views and various detail sheets but NO cross-section drawings are provided that specifically show vertical clearances at transformer pad access paths. The site has buildings on multiple levels with various finished floor elevations (ranging from 683.0' to 687.50' per Sheet 21), but there are no cross-sections showing the vertical space available for hot-stick access (35 feet clearance for standard access, or higher for specific confined situations). No vertical clearance profile is provided for any of the five transformer pad locations.
findings.reasoning: Austin Energy Design typically requires cross-section drawings to verify vertical clearances at transformer pad access paths, particularly where overhead structures, building elements, or uneven topography could restrict clearance for equipment access and operation. Without these cross-sections, vertical clearance compliance cannot be verified. This is a standard documentation requirement for complete electrical site plan design.

findings.comment: Cross-section drawings showing vertical clearances at transformer pad locations are not provided on the site plan. For each transformer pad location where overhead structures, building elements, or parking structures are present above or adjacent to the pad, provide cross-section drawings (drawn at adequate scale and clearly labeled) demonstrating the required vertical clearances from the pad to any overhead features.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations with potential overhead structures, parking garages, or enclosed areas
findings.observation: Review of all 39 sheets in the primary site plan revealed no cross-section drawings specifically showing vertical clearances at transformer pad locations. The site plan shows buildings with various heights (33'-5" to 36'-1"), parking levels, and enclosed structures, but no cross-sections are provided to demonstrate vertical clearance compliance at transformer locations. The general notes reference cross-section requirements for other utilities (e.g., drainage, conveyance), but no cross-sections are provided specifically showing vertical clearances from transformer pads to overhead structures, parking garage levels, or enclosed areas.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 establishes survey and design requirements for clearances from AE facilities to structures. Transformer pads located between buildings or adjacent to parking areas (particularly Pad 4 between Bldgs 4-5, and Pad 5 near parking) warrant vertical clearance verification through cross-section drawings. The absence of any cross-section drawings showing vertical clearances at these locations is a clear failure to document compliance with this requirement. The code requires demonstrating that overhead structures, building eaves, or parking structures do not create vertical clearance violations.

findings.comment: Transformer pads NW of Building 1 and W of Building 2 are located within 4 feet of vehicle circulation driveways but lack bollard callouts and specifications. Provide bollard details and callouts on the site plan for all transformer pads within 4 feet of parking or vehicle routes, with specifications matching AE Design-approved pad details.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad NW of Building 1 (within 4 feet of entry driveway)
Transformer pad W of Building 2 (within 4 feet of internal driveway)
Transformer pad W of Building 8 (within 4 feet of internal driveway - status to be confirmed)
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows all five transformer pads located immediately adjacent to vehicle circulation routes (driveways). Vision analysis confirmed that pads NW of Bldg 1, W of Bldg 2, W of Bldg 8, E of Bldg 4, and E of Bldg 7 are all within or very near the 4-foot threshold from vehicle circulation areas. The measure-distance tool confirmed the pad NW of Bldg 1 is 0 feet from the driveway edge (touching the driveway). Sheet 9 shows bollard callouts (labeled 'Bollard (Typ)') pointing to features at two locations: E of Bldg 4 and E of Bldg 7. These two pads have bollard protection documented. HOWEVER, the pads at NW of Bldg 1 and W of Bldg 2 are equally constrained by proximity to vehicle circulation but show NO bollard callouts or detail references on the site plan.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 specifies that equipment pads installed within 4 feet of parking areas or vehicle routes must be protected by 4-inch minimum diameter galvanized rigid metal posts (bollards) per AE Design equipment pad details, with spacing that allows equipment door opening. The site plan clearly shows two of five transformer pads (E of Bldg 4 and E of Bldg 7) with bollard protection documented via callouts. However, the other three pads (NW of Bldg 1, W of Bldg 2, and W of Bldg 8) are equally exposed to vehicle circulation (based on spatial layout) but lack any bollard documentation. This represents an inconsistency and likely non-compliance for the unprotected pads. At minimum, the pads at NW of Bldg 1 and W of Bldg 2 require bollard documentation.

findings.comment: Transformer Pad 5, located within 4 feet of a parking/circulation drive lane, requires bollard protection. No bollard specifications, locations, or details are shown on the electrical plan or construction details. Provide dimension callouts and detail references (per AE Design equipment pad details) showing 4-inch minimum diameter galvanized rigid metal bollards installed to protect the transformer pad, with spacing that allows equipment door opening.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 and visual analysis show Pad 5 located in the southeast section of the site, positioned approximately 2-5 feet north of the southern driveway/parking lane. The Fire Protection Plan (Sheet 10) shows this area is part of the main circulation and parking zone. The code requires bollards (4-inch minimum diameter galvanized rigid metal posts) when transformer pads are installed within 4 feet of parking areas or vehicle routes. Pad 5's estimated 2-5 foot distance from the parking drive lane indicates it falls within the 4-foot bollard requirement threshold. However, no bollard specifications, locations, or detail references are shown on the site plan.
findings.reasoning: Based on visual analysis, Pad 5 is estimated to be 2-5 feet from a parking drive lane, placing it within the 4-foot triggering distance for bollard installation. The absence of any bollard callouts, specifications, or detail references on the electrical plan or construction details sheets suggests the requirement is not being addressed. Without explicit bollard documentation showing their location, spacing, and specifications per AE Design equipment pad details, compliance cannot be verified.

findings.comment: Transformer pad locations not coordinated with water line routing on unified plan. Provide dimensioned utility coordination drawing showing transformer pads and water lines with documented 5-foot horizontal clearances.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations relative to water infrastructure
findings.observation: Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows three transformer pad locations but does not depict water line routing or utility conflicts. Utility tap plan (Sheet 19) shows water line infrastructure (2" HDPE private domestic water branches and 6" main water lines) but does not depict transformer pad locations (transformer pads shown only on electrical sheet, not on utility sheet). While both utilities are shown on different sheets, no overlay or cross-reference plan is provided documenting distances between transformer pads and water lines.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 2.9.1.B.2 requires minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance between transformer pads and water lines. Without a coordinated drawing showing both transformer pads and water line routing simultaneously with dimensional measurements, clearances cannot be verified. The separation of transformer pads (on electrical sheet) from water infrastructure (on utility sheet) without a coordination overlay prevents documentation of compliance.

findings.comment: Transformer pad locations not coordinated with wastewater line routing on unified plan. Provide dimensioned utility coordination drawing showing transformer pads and wastewater lines with documented 5-foot horizontal clearances.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations relative to wastewater infrastructure
findings.observation: Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows three transformer pads but does not show wastewater line routing. Utility tap plan (Sheet 19) shows wastewater infrastructure (6" PVC wastewater branches at 2.0% minimum slope, lift station, cleanouts) but transformer pads are not depicted on this utility sheet. No overlay drawing provided showing both utilities simultaneously with dimensional clearance measurements.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 2.9.1.B.2 requires minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance between transformer pads and wastewater lines. Separation of these utilities on different sheets without a coordination drawing showing distances prevents verification of compliance.

findings.comment: Transformer Pad 3 shown directly on top of storm drain line on electrical design plan. This violates the minimum 5-foot clearance requirement. Relocate transformer pad to avoid storm drain infrastructure, or modify storm drain routing with documented approval. Provide revised electrical and drainage plans showing minimum 5-foot clearance between transformer pad edge and storm drain line.
applicableAreas: Transformer Pad 3 located in central courtyard area
findings.observation: Vision analysis of electrical design plan (Sheet 21) explicitly states: "The transformer pad symbol is drawn directly on top of an underground line labeled `SD` (Storm Drain). It is also adjacent to an underground electrical line route." This places Transformer Pad 3 directly overlapping the storm drain infrastructure shown on the electrical plan. Storm drain plan (Sheet 12) would document storm drain line routing in greater detail. Utility coordination between electrical and drainage systems is required to address this overlap.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 2.9.1.B.2 requires minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from transformer pads to storm drain lines. The vision analysis clearly confirms that Transformer Pad 3 is positioned on top of (zero clearance from) the storm drain line marked "SD" on the electrical design plan. This represents a complete failure to maintain the required 5-foot clearance and indicates either: (1) the transformer pad location is incorrectly placed, or (2) the storm drain routing conflicts with the intended transformer pad location. This conflict must be resolved by relocating either the pad or the storm drain line.

findings.comment: Transformer Pad 3 overlaps underground storm drain line, providing zero clearance instead of required minimum 12 inches (horizontal and vertical). Revise design to relocate transformer pad outside of storm drain infrastructure or reroute storm drain to achieve minimum 12-inch clearance on all sides.
applicableAreas: Transformer Pad 3 located over storm drain line
findings.observation: Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows Transformer Pad 3 positioned on top of underground storm drain line marked "SD" per vision analysis. This represents zero clearance in both horizontal and vertical dimensions from the storm drain infrastructure. UCM § 1.10.5.A requires minimum 12-inch horizontal and vertical clearance from all underground utilities except those specifically exempted (gas, fuel, steam).
findings.reasoning: The overlapping of Transformer Pad 3 on the storm drain line (SD) shown on the electrical design plan demonstrates complete failure to maintain the minimum 12-inch horizontal and vertical clearance required by UCM § 1.10.5.A. A transformer pad cannot be constructed directly over an underground storm drain line without creating structural and utility conflicts. This represents a design deficiency requiring resolution through pad relocation or utility rerouting.

findings.comment: Transformer Pad 3 shown positioned over storm drain line, which violates prohibition against utilities crossing without approval. Provide documentation of written approval from City of Austin Watershed Protection Department and Austin Energy Design authorizing this utility crossing, or relocate transformer pad outside storm drain infrastructure.
applicableAreas: Transformer Pad 3 located in central courtyard area
findings.observation: Vision analysis of electrical design plan (Sheet 21) confirms: "The transformer pad symbol is drawn directly on top of an underground line labeled `SD` (Storm Drain)." This indicates that Transformer Pad 3 is positioned to cross over storm drain utility infrastructure. The pad footprint (shown as a dotted rectangle) appears to be placed directly within the storm drain line routing.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.B prohibits locating transformer pads or Austin Energy underground facilities over or under other utility lines without written approval from the appropriate utility authority. The positioning of Transformer Pad 3 on top of the storm drain line represents a crossing/overlay configuration that violates this requirement. If utilities must cross, it requires documented written approval from both the stormwater utility (City of Austin Watershed Protection) and Austin Energy. No such approval documentation is provided in the site plan submittal.

findings.comment: Cross-section drawings not provided showing vertical clearances around transformer pads. Provide cross-section drawings through Transformer Pad 3 location demonstrating adequate vertical clearance for equipment access, maintenance, and operation; confirm no structures are positioned directly above pad.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations, particularly Transformer Pad 3 in central courtyard
findings.observation: Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows transformer pads as simple dotted rectangles. Site plan (Sheet 9) shows general building layout without transformer detail. Grading plan (Sheet 11) shows site topography and building elevation profiles. However, no cross-section drawings or vertical clearance profiles are provided showing: (1) vertical clearances in the central courtyard area where Transformer Pad 3 is surrounded by multi-story buildings (Buildings 4, 5, 6), (2) overhead obstructions or structures above the transformer pad locations, or (3) vertical clearances for crane/equipment access.
findings.reasoning: No cross-section drawings showing vertical clearances around transformer pads are provided in the plan set. For Transformer Pad 3 especially, which is surrounded by buildings and located in a courtyard area, vertical clearance documentation is required to demonstrate that: (1) no structures hang directly above the pad, (2) adequate clearance exists for equipment maintenance and replacement, (3) proper ventilation is available if niche configuration applies, and (4) liquid drainage paths exist if oil-filled equipment.

findings.comment: Transformer Pad 3 located in parking/circulation area without bollard protection shown. Provide detailed electrical or site plan showing 4-inch minimum diameter galvanized rigid metal bollards positioned around Transformer Pad 3 to prevent vehicle contact. Bollard spacing must allow pad access door to open fully per Austin Energy Design equipment pad standards.
applicableAreas: Transformer Pad 3 located in central parking/circulation area
findings.observation: Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows Transformer Pad 3 positioned in the central courtyard area described as "located within an open paved/drive area surrounded by the three aforementioned buildings." Site plan (Sheet 9) shows this central area includes parking and circulation areas with driveways. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 states: "Bollards or protection barriers: None are shown or labeled." Construction details (Sheet 22) include bollard specifications per COA standards but no bollards are called out or dimensioned on the electrical plan for the transformer pad areas.
findings.reasoning: Transformer Pad 3 is positioned in the central site area that serves as a parking/circulation zone between Buildings 4, 5, and 6. This location puts the pad within the 4-foot proximity zone that triggers bollard requirements. No bollards are shown on any plan sheets protecting this pad from vehicle contact. Bollard placement and spacing must be shown on electrical/site plans to prevent accidental vehicle impact on the transformer equipment.
